title: Field boundary delineation with seasonal sentinel 2 imagery using Segment Anything Model (SAM)
author: Ha, Nketia, et al.

steps.title: Create Python environments
steps.instruction: Install the free Anaconda distribution on Windows, create two separate conda environments, and install required libraries: • Environment for downloading Sentinel‑2 imagery (named rgb‑environment) – run `conda env create -f environment.yml` then `conda activate rgb-environment`. • Environment for segmentation (named field‑boundary‑seg) – open the ArcGIS Pro Python Command Prompt, run `conda create --name field-boundary-seg --clone arcgispro-py3` then `conda activate field-boundary-seg`. Both environments use Python 3.10.18 (Anaconda 4.14.0). Install geemap v0.20.6, GDAL v3.4.3, and the Google Earth Engine API v0.1.355. Ensure a GEE account is created at https://code.earthengine.google.com.

substeps.instruction: Install Anaconda on Windows.
Create and activate the rgb‑environment for image download.
Create and activate the field‑boundary‑seg environment by cloning arcgispro‑py3.
Install geemap v0.20.6, GDAL v3.4.3, and GEE API v0.1.355 in the respective environments.

steps.title: Acquire and preprocess Sentinel‑2 images
steps.instruction: In JupyterLab open the notebook `2_RGB_download/1a_rgb_download.ipynb`, set the region of interest (province), target years 2021‑2024, and an output folder. Run the script to: • Retrieve Sentinel‑2 collections via the GEE Python API for months May‑September, filtering out scenes with ≥50 % cloud cover. • Apply a census‑subdivision tiling system to clip images per tile. • For each tile, median‑compose three seasonal bands: Red (May–July, band B4), Green (July–August, band B3), Blue (August–September, band B2). • Stack the three bands, clip to the tile geometry, and convert to 8‑bit Uint8 (`s2img = ee.Image(s2jun.addBands(s2jul).addBands(s2aug)).clip(tilesub.geometry()).toUint8()`). • Mosaic the yearly images, mask remaining non‑cropland using Otsu thresholding, and generate a cropland boundary shapefile. Masking also incorporates ESA WorldCover 10 m, the AAFC crop inventory map, and the Statistics Canada road network.

substeps.instruction: Configure notebook parameters (ROI, years, output path).
Run GEE API calls to download images with <50 % cloud cover.
Perform tile‑based clipping and median compositing for Red (B4), Green (B3), Blue (B2).
Stack bands, clip to tile, convert to Uint8.
Mosaic annually, apply Otsu threshold mask, produce cropland shapefile.
Integrate ESA WorldCover, AAFC crop inventory, and road network for final masking.

steps.title: Segment fields with SAM
steps.instruction: Open notebook `3_Segmentation/3a_arcpy_rgb_segmentation.ipynb` in the segmentation environment. Update file paths to point to the 8‑bit RGB GeoTIFF (`inRaster`), the output shapefile (`outFeature`), and the pre‑trained SAM model file `SAM.dlpk` (`sam`). Define the SAM parameters as follows: Padding = 256, Batch‑size = 4, Box_nms_thresh = 0.7, Points_per_batch = 64, Stability_score_thres = 0.95, Min_mask_region_area = 0, Run_nms = 'NMS', Confidence_score_field = 'Confidence', Class_value_field = 'Class'. Execute the ArcPy deep‑learning call `arcpy.ia.DetectObjectsUsingDeepLearning(inRaster, outFeature, sam, parameters)`. Apply the model to either each yearly RGB composite or to a single multi‑year averaged RGB composite.

substeps.instruction: Edit notebook to set paths for input raster, output feature class, and SAM model.
Enter the parameter table values listed above.
Run `arcpy.ia.DetectObjectsUsingDeepLearning` to generate candidate masks.
Retain high‑confidence masks and export them as field‑polygon shapefiles.

steps.title: Clean and refine polygons
steps.instruction: Run `4a_arcpy_clean_shp.ipynb` to perform the first cleaning stage: • Intersect multi‑year inputs to align coincident edges and resolve topology. • Explode multipart features. • Compute geodesic area and discard polygons smaller than 2 ha. • Count overlaps to flag ambiguous boundaries. • Apply an inward buffer of –20 m to trim spikes and narrow artifacts, then recompute area. • Filter again to keep only polygons ≥2 ha. • Apply an outward buffer of +20 m to restore original scale and save the cleaned shapefile. Then run `4b_cropmask.ipynb` for the second stage: • Intersect the cleaned polygons with the AAFC crop mask. • Compute the zonal mean of the crop‑mask values for each polygon and write this value to a new attribute. • Remove polygons whose mean crop‑mask value is <0.4, retaining only fields with a majority cropland signal.

substeps.instruction: Intersect inputs, explode multipart features, compute area.
Remove polygons <2 ha.
Count overlaps, apply –20 m inward buffer, recompute area.
Filter polygons ≥2 ha, apply +20 m outward buffer, save cleaned shapefile.
Intersect cleaned polygons with AAFC crop mask.
Calculate zonal mean crop‑mask value per polygon.
Delete polygons with mean <0.4.

steps.title: Assess segmentation accuracy
steps.instruction: Select 15 random locations across the Canadian Prairies covering approximately 260.57 ha (643.84 ac). For each location compute the Intersection over Union (IoU) between the segmented field polygons and manually digitized reference boundaries. Record the overall mean IoU (0.86) and province‑level means: Saskatchewan 0.85 (107.95 ha), Alberta 0.89 (60.43 ha), Manitoba 0.86 (92.19 ha).

substeps.instruction: Randomly sample 15 validation sites (~260.57 ha total).
Calculate IoU for each site between SAM output and reference polygons.
Aggregate results to obtain overall and provincial mean IoU values.
